description: A sibling of plugin-host with the same size and shape, at version 0.9.2, where four practices are done right and a report that flags them is wrong: a lint baseline that CI keeps from growing, a release flag with an owner, an expiry, and tests in both states, an option removed in a 0.y.z release with a changelog note, and an issue workflow that passes the title through an environment variable. Three ordinary gaps remain.

must_find.CI-02: ci.yml pins actions/checkout and actions/setup-python to version tags instead of commit SHAs
must_find.ARCH-05: run in loader.py catches every exception and returns None, so a failing plugin leaves no trace and the command exits with 0
must_find.SEC-07: the library is published on PyPI, but there is no SECURITY.md or other channel for reporting a vulnerability

must_not_flag.QUAL-05: tools/docstring-baseline.json lists the violations that predate the docstring rule with a reason, an owner, and a removal condition; tools/check_docstrings.py fails CI when a violation is added or a fixed one stays listed, and on a pull request when the baseline gains an entry beside any other change; an entry alone fails as not a violation, so the baseline cannot grow and no blanket ignore exists
must_not_flag.STRUCT-04: skip_private_files is a release flag with a purpose, an owner, and an expiry date in pluginhost/flags.py, and the tests run discovery with the flag off and on
must_not_flag.DEL-03: the package is at 0.9.2, where any release may change the interface, and the 0.9.0 entry of the changelog notes the removal of the --format option; releases are versioned, recorded, and approved by a second maintainer
must_not_flag.CI-10: the issue workflow passes the title through the TITLE environment variable and quotes it, so event data never becomes script text; nothing runs untrusted code, and CI has no secrets and does not publish
must_not_flag.TOOL-01: no tools, skills, or MCP servers configured

defects.description: ci.yml pins both actions to version tags instead of commit SHAs
run catches every exception and returns None, so a failing plugin is invisible
